clue.text: Fire people in competition

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A boss lays off staff for being too competitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a children's sports-day contest in which runners hop along inside sacks.

clue.text: Offer accommodation and bustle about

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word are moved around

explanation.surface: A landlady rushes about getting rooms ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant who sublets lets the property, or part of it, to someone else.

clue.text: Artful lamentation about a certain measure taken

indicators.note: about means the word for lamentation goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a cry is a wail of grief
ft is the abbreviation for foot, a unit of length

explanation.surface: A cunning complaint about someone's measurements being taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain measure' looks like one idea, but it splits into the article and an abbreviated unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful and crafty both mean cunning, skilled at deceit.

clue.text: Retiring military men did what military men do

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
soldiers serve in the forces

explanation.surface: Veterans leaving the army who had done their duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, reserved person is withdrawn and keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Some approach a tutor just to talk

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some students go to their tutor only for a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation, talking for its own sake.

clue.text: Bound to season

explanation.surface: Someone is destined to add salt and pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound is to leap or jump forward; the season between winter and summer has the same name.

clue.text: Compound for terriers in grand environment

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for grand

parts.note: posh means grand or upper-class
terriers are Territorial Army soldiers, abbreviated TA

explanation.surface: Treatment for dogs in an upmarket setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' are not dogs here but Territorial Army volunteers, Britain's army reserve; the surface pictures pet treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound used in fertiliser and soap.

clue.text: She is a beautiful Italian

parts.note: taken as written
bella is Italian for beautiful

explanation.surface: A woman described as a lovely Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's name, so it stands for 'she', any female person.

clue.text: Laggards model the finest clothes

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Slowcoaches showing off couture on the catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is informal for one's best outfit, worn for a special occasion.

clue.text: General cash cover

parts.note: brass is old British slang for money
a hat covers the head

explanation.surface: An instruction about insuring money in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is slang for a high-ranking officer, from the gold braid on senior officers' caps.

clue.text: Classes making tarts-a disaster!

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A baking session where the pastries come out as a complete failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a disaster' signals the anagram of TARTS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, used figuratively for social levels or ranks.

clue.text: Reduces discounts

explanation.surface: A shop cuts its prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebate is to lessen or blunt; rebates are refunds or price reductions.

clue.text: It's no longer wrong to apply the squeeze

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone decides pressuring others is now acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the squeeze on someone is to force money or concessions from them by pressure.

clue.text: Mature folk curse such gear

parts.note: adult males are men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Grown men grumble about the clothes they are made to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing sold for males, the kind of gear worn by the grown men the clue mentions.

clue.text: Magnificently arranged gallery

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art gallery has been splendidly laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in a royal, splendid manner.

clue.text: Quite a few part with almost everything

parts.note: to part is to sever or separate

indicators.note: almost means the word for everything loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a good many of their possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, a modest number.

clue.text: Young women turning over waste material

indicators.note: turning over says the word for young women is read backwards

parts.note: gals is informal for girls or young women

explanation.surface: Girls flipping through a rubbish heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Slag is the waste left after smelting ore, also mining spoil.

clue.text: A minister's frugal tea?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain means simple and frugal

explanation.surface: A clergyman's modest afternoon refreshment.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a school or regiment.

clue.text: Flashy dispute with the top man

parts.note: to spar is to argue
the king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A showy argument with the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparking throws off sparks, flashing brightly.

clue.text: A large number are into quiet music

indicators.note: into means the earlier pieces go inside the word for quiet

parts.note: serene means calm and quiet
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Many people take to playing soft music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts A and D inside SERENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music sung or played, often at night, to a loved one.

clue.text: The expectation of a man without work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the man goes around the work

parts.note: he refers to a man
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: What an unemployed man looks forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: HE goes outside OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a feeling of anticipation that something wished for will happen.

clue.text: Risked earnings with an embarrassed look

parts.note: a wage is what one earns
turning red is how embarrassment shows

explanation.surface: A gambler who blushes after betting their pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To wager is to bet, putting money at risk.

clue.text: Placed around a church, this smells delightful

indicators.note: around means the word for placed goes around the other pieces

parts.note: set means placed

explanation.surface: Something put round a church that gives off a lovely fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's closing phrase, describing a scented object, so the surface nearly reads as one description.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small scented bag laid among clothes to perfume them.

clue.text: A foreign town worker has to go after a row

indicators.note: has to go after says the worker is placed following the row

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a row
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: An overseas labourer must leave following a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinant is a town in Belgium on the river Meuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinant is a Belgian town on the Meuse, foreign from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Guard appearing fed-up over a tip

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word fed is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
the end is the tip

explanation.surface: A sentry seems weary of a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'fed-up' reads as weary, but splits into a word and its reversal signal ('up', fitting a down clue).
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect from attack.

clue.text: Soft golden furniture may well be moved

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
or is the heraldic word for gold
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Gilded, delicate furniture that someone wants relocating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable is light enough to be carried about easily.

clue.text: Explain appalling need if required

indicators.note: appalling suggests something badly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an account of a dreadful shortage if necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' signals the anagram of NEED IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to state its meaning precisely.

clue.text: Married before — must be simple!

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone who has wed earlier should keep things plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, plain and simple.

clue.text: A Conservative must be correct

parts.note: the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: A party loyalist insists a Tory is always in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Aright means properly, rightly, without error.

clue.text: Stuff about English standard set at intervals

indicators.note: about means the word for stuff goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to stuff oneself is to sate
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: Instructions for filling something to a common English norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun meaning material, but it is the verb meaning to fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed apart from one another are kept distinct, with gaps between them.

clue.text: Dark times — things have changed

indicators.note: have changed says the letters of the word before it take a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy era in which everything has shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have changed' signals the anagram of THINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness each day are night-time.

clue.text: Let out about direction being objected to

indicators.note: about here means the word for let out goes around the compass point

parts.note: a property let out is rented
SE, south-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A landlord leased a flat about which tenants complained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as releasing, but it is the landlord's sense of leasing a property.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation at it.
